verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents a Bayesian statistics approach for experiment decision-making, and it highlights a leading variation when there is not yet enough data to declare a winner. That covers the 'documented statistics engine' core of the story. However, the evidence says nothing about variance-reduction options, a frequentist alternative, or how the engine works. missing for 10: variance-reduction options (e.g. CUPED), frequentist methodology option, in-depth statistical methodology documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can trust a documented statistics engine (Bayesian or frequentist, with variance-reduction options) behind experiment results

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly highlights the leading variation when there is not yet enough experiment data to declare a winning variation.
